How to use this tracker

A study tracker for HSC Physics, Chemistry, Higher Math and Biology. It tracks where you are; it does not grade you. Exam scores are the only real measurement, and they live in Exam files.

The top of the page
  • Rank banner: your rank (of 37), your shards and how many more you need for the next rank.
  • Wallet: Tanzanite shards (of 10,000) and Stardust, plus the Marketplace and Backup buttons.
  • Tabs: Overview, Syllabus, one per subject, Study log, Exam files and To revise.
  • Bottom left: this guide and the focus sounds (bird icon). Bottom right: the calendar and the timer.
Tracking a subject
  • Weights: each chapter has importance, difficulty and volume ratings (1 to 5). Importance counts most (40%), then volume (35%), then difficulty (25%). They set the chapter’s “% of paper”, so a heavy chapter moves your progress more. The ratings are starting guesses, so change them under each chapter.
  • Completed slider: drag it to how much of the chapter you have covered, in steps of 5%.
  • Four practice boxes: Theory, CQ test papers, MCQ solve, ক, খ practice. Each tick adds a quarter of proficiency for that chapter. Covering a chapter and being able to score on it are different things.
  • Needs revision: flag a chapter and it appears in the To revise tab. Untick it there once you have revised it.
  • Strips: each block is a chapter and its width is its share of the paper. Top strip is coverage, green bottom strip is proficiency.
  • Covered is syllabus done, weighted. Proficient is coverage scaled by the practice boxes. Proficiency ratio is proficient divided by covered; a low ratio means you read a lot but practised little.
Overview tab

Shows totals across all four subjects, then a card per subject. Each subject counts equally, and both papers count equally within a subject. “Reset all progress” clears coverage sliders and practice ticks only. Your study log, exam files and purchases are not touched.

Study log
  • By hand: enter hours (up to 24, steps of 0.25) and a date, say what you studied, and from your second log onward choose Better, About the same or Worse than your last log.
  • With the timer: it fills the log for you.
  • Only one entry per date. A second session on the same day is added to that day’s entry.
  • You also get a bar chart (7, 14, 30 or 90 days), all-time hours, daily average, best day, streak and a history list where you can delete entries.
The timer
  • Study: stopwatch or countdown. When you stop, say what you studied and it is saved to your log. Pause, resume or discard any time.
  • Break: a rest timer. Nothing is logged.
  • Spendature: pick an item you bought in the Marketplace and it counts down. The item is marked used when you start; if you cancel, it returns to My items.
  • Countdowns beep and vibrate at the end. The timer keeps running if you close the tab, and the live time shows in the tab title. Sessions under a minute are not logged.
The two currencies

Tanzanite shards come only from syllabus coverage. There are 10,000 in total, 2,500 per subject. You never spend them, and they decide your rank.

Stardust comes from study hours. Each log pays hours × 800 × (0.5 + how that day compares with your best day). Your first log sets the baseline. A Better day raises your standard by 15%, a Worse day lowers it by 15%, About the same leaves it. Beating your own peak day gives a 1.5× bonus. That is roughly 1,000 Stardust per good hour.

Marketplace
  • Spend Stardust on rewards you choose. A few defaults come included, and you can add your own.
  • Once you add an item, its price cannot be changed or removed. That is on purpose, so you cannot haggle with yourself.
  • Bought items go to My items. Press Use when you take the reward.
Exam files

Make a file for an exam series, such as “Physics model tests”, open it and add each exam with a name, a score (any format, like 38/50) and a date. Nothing in the game uses these scores, so they stay an honest record.

Calendar and tasks
  • Tap the calendar icon (next to the timer). The badge shows how many tasks are still open today.
  • Pick a day in the month grid. Dots under a date mean it has tasks.
  • Add a task: title, optional time, optional note and a colour. Tick it when done, edit it () to change the text or move it to another date, or delete it.
  • Coming up lists your next open tasks and warns you about overdue ones. Tap one to jump to its day.
  • Choose which day the week starts on with the button at the bottom. Calendar tasks are included in Backup.
Focus sounds
  • Tap the bird icon at the bottom left. Tap a track to play it on loop and tap it again to stop it.
  • Ambient: ocean, rain, casual guitar, birds in a woodland and white noise.
  • Lofi: over 100 different lofi tracks.
  • You can play more than one at once, for example rain with a lofi track. The volume slider controls everything.
  • The sounds are generated live by your browser, not played from recordings, so they work offline and loop with no gap. Your browser only allows sound after you tap something, so music never starts by itself.
The bunny

A small bunny hops in every few minutes with a short motivational line, then leaves. Tap the bunny for another one, or tap Dismiss. It never touches your data.

Backup (important)

Everything is saved only in your own browser. Clearing browser data or switching device wipes it. Use Backup to export a file, or copy it as text, and Import to restore. Importing replaces everything on the page.

A simple routine
  1. Adjust the chapter ratings you disagree with, once.
  2. Move the Completed slider and tick the practice boxes you have really done.
  3. Use the timer for study sessions, or log them by hand afterwards.
  4. Flag shaky chapters as Needs revision.
  5. Log every mock or test in Exam files.
  6. Export a backup now and then.

Be honest with the sliders. They are self-reported, so the tool is only as accurate as you are. Open the file in Chrome, Edge or Safari, not inside a chat app’s preview.
